_meta.purpose: Privacy templates: six classified by the LINDDUN privacy-threat taxonomy (LINDDUN (c) KU Leuven, see src/lib/privacy/linddun.ts) and ten from the OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks (c) OWASP, CC-BY-SA, paraphrased and attributed by the [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks] marker, never the verbatim OWASP text. frameworkTag points at a NIST Privacy Framework subcategory.
_meta.origin: Moved verbatim from the inline `privacyRiskTemplates` array in prisma/seed.ts (2026-11-08), so production receives it: prisma/seed.ts is never run on a deploy.
_meta.deliveredBy: scripts/seed-risk-templates.ts on every container start (scripts/entrypoint.sh), and prisma/seed.ts in dev, both through prisma/risk-template-fixtures.ts.

templates.title: Re-identification of De-identified Data
templates.description: Individuals are singled out or re-identified from data that was meant to be anonymous or pseudonymous.

templates.title: Excessive Data Linking
templates.description: Records meant to stay separate are correlated, building a fuller profile of an individual than any single source intended.

templates.title: Unlawful or Non-compliant Processing
templates.description: Personal data is processed without a valid legal basis or outside the bounds of applicable privacy regulation.

templates.title: Excessive Data Collection and Disclosure
templates.description: More personal data is collected, stored, or shared than necessary for the stated purpose.

templates.title: Lack of Transparency and Data-Subject Control
templates.description: Individuals are unaware of how their data is processed and cannot exercise access, correction, deletion, or consent-withdrawal rights.

templates.title: Covert Tracking and Behavioral Detection
templates.description: An individual's presence or activity is inferred from observable side effects without their awareness.

templates.title: Web Application Vulnerability Leading to Data Breach
templates.description: A web-application security flaw is exploited to expose personal data. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Operator-Sided Data Leakage
templates.description: Personal data leaks through the operator's own systems, staff, or processes rather than an external attack. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Insufficient Data Breach Response
templates.description: The organization detects, handles, or notifies individuals of a privacy breach too slowly or incompletely. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Overbroad or Bundled Consent
templates.description: Consent is requested for everything at once rather than granular, purpose-specific choices. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Non-Transparent Policies and Terms
templates.description: Privacy policies and terms are unclear, hard to find, or do not reflect actual data practices. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Insufficient Deletion of Personal Data
templates.description: Personal data is retained beyond its purpose or not fully deleted on request or expiry. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Insufficient Data Quality
templates.description: Outdated or inaccurate personal data leads to wrong decisions about individuals. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Missing or Insufficient Session Expiration
templates.description: Sessions exposing personal data are not expired, leaving data accessible on shared or lost devices. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Inability of Users to Access and Modify Data
templates.description: Individuals cannot view, correct, or export the personal data held about them. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]

templates.title: Collection of Data Not Required for the Primary Purpose
templates.description: Personal data unrelated to the service's primary purpose is collected and retained. [OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks]
